content: @kanaries/graphic-walker latest stable dist-tag is 0.5.2 (0.5.0-alpha.x line stabilized). Simple integration: <GraphicWalker dataSource={rows: IRow[]} rawFields={fields: IMutField[]} />, with no computation prop needed for client-side use (default computation runs in-browser). For large/remote datasets it also supports a computation prop: async (query: IDataQueryPayload) => IRow[], enabling a custom engine. Official Kanaries platform doc 'Use Duckdb-wasm for computation in GraphicWalker' shows using @kanaries/gw-dsl-parser + @duckdb/duckdb-wasm together: register data as a table in DuckDB, convert GraphicWalker's query payload to SQL via parser_dsl_with_table(), run it, convert Arrow result back to IRow[] via transformData()/ArrowToJSON(). This is recommended only for large datasets; for typical survey-sized data (thousands of rows) simplest path is to query parquet once via DuckDB-Wasm, materialize to a JS array + field list, and pass directly as dataSource/rawFields.
